answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors now risks onboarding friction and delivery interruption right when there's zero slack to absorb it—memory_c2's quick-onboarding case didn't carry this volume-pressure context. Renewing outright (memory_c1) preserves stability but doesn't address the mandated 18% spend cut. Negotiating at renewal (memory_c4) offers a path to recover real margin and improve payment terms while keeping the same integration and delivery schedule intact, directly serving the TCO-without-risk objective. I want to verify memory_c4 and memory_c1 before committing since they jointly justify this middle path and I need to confirm the renegotiation case actually involved comparable volume/urgency conditions rather than a slack-time scenario. This is treated as the standard course of action for the current renewal cycle rather than a small test or a broad structural change, since it applies to the existing primary contract only. Risk flagged: a 14-day window may be too short to fully negotiate an 18%-equivalent reduction, so if talks stall, the next cycle should reassess switch_primary_vendor or add_second_source before assuming this fully closes the cost gap.
